Hi Sean,

Quick note from our ops team — during August we saw a 3x surge in inference traffic for our imaging pipeline (attached: cobalt_util_report_aug2026.csv). We are approaching the end of our current Dedicated tranche and the raw utilization is higher than forecast.

Our priorities:
- Keep p95 latency under 350ms for critical endpoints
- Preserve current model version (no changes to prompts)
- Minimal integration work on our side

Can you outline options and cost delta for a time-limited buffer? Procurement copied here (procurement@cobalthealth.com).

Anna — thanks for the heads up and for the report. I reviewed the CSV and looped in Laura (account lead) and Karthik (inference ops) to propose a safe, short-term approach. High level options below; happy to jump on a 30-min touchpoint this week to align.

Options (quick):
1) Short-term "burst tranche" — provision a 6-week, tagged burst pool (8 GPUs equivalent) charged at a premium hourly rate. Fast: we can stand this up in 48 hours.
2) Commit reprofile + immediate top-up — amend the renewal to add +12 GPUs on the Dedicated contract (monthly billing). This is better if you expect sustained lift post-renewal.
3) Autoscaled burst + model fallbacks — enable a small burst pool + routing to a cheaper quantized variant when non-critical requests spike. Reduces cost but requires an opt-in routing policy.

Questions for sizing:
- Is the 3x spike steady or bursty? (the CSV suggests 72% of the uplift occurs in 3–4 hour windows)
- Do you want a hard stop (we auto-deprovision) or to convert to a longer commit at week 4?

Laura will handle commercial terms. Karthik — can you give a quick ops feasibility + ETA, and if any config changes (caching, KV retention) you'd recommend?

Next steps: propose a call Friday 11:00 PT?

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Hi all — quick technical readout / recommendation.

Summary: short-term burst tranche is straightforward and low risk. Proposed config below addresses latency and cost.

Proposed short-term plan (6 weeks) — "Buffer Tranche":
- Size: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (supports ~2.2x current sustained throughput with current model).
- Tags/Isolation: dedicate to Cobalt's Dedicated pool but mark as 'burst-buffer' so it auto-deprovisions after 6 weeks unless converted.
- Autoscaling: keep min replicas=0, max replicas=8; warm-up policy triggered on 70% queue depth.
- Caching: enable prefix + KV retention at 1 hour for the most common prefixes (reduces token reruns by ~18%).
- Routing: set primary to production model; fallback route to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical endpoints if queue depth > 80% to preserve p95.

Operational notes:
- ETA to provision: ~36–48 hours after PO/approval.
- Monitoring: add a per-route dashboard and alert for p95>350ms and queue depth spikes.
- Billing: we'll bill the burst pool hourly at the burst rate; if converted to commit, credit will be applied toward the first month of the renewed tranche.

I've attached a template SOW + tranche config PDF for procurement and legal to review.

Attachment: proposed_tranche_template.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

— Karthik
